newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, May 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, May 21.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Wednesday.
- The Labour Party's decision to focus its 1.5 billion Irish pound tax package on lower and middle-income earners will be non-negotiable in discussions on the formation of a new government.
- Five Irish beaches have failed to meet European Union bathing-water quality standards.
- Marks & Spencer is planning a 12 million Irish pound expansion of one of its stores in Dublin.

- Waterford Co-op, which is still considering a takeover offer from Avonmore Co-op, has cut the price it pays its milk suppliers by a penny per gallon for deliveries in April. The cut brings the price paid by Waterford to 4-1/4p below that offered by Avonmore.
- The main opposition party, Fianna Fail, is standing by its tax plans despite claims that they are weighted in favour of the better-paid.
- Two republican prisoners in Britain will return to Northern Ireland to serve the rest of their sentences.

- SDLP leader John Hume and his Ulster Unionist counterpart David Trimble are to hold urgent talks on the parades issue. - Ireland should take the inflationary risk of joining a single European currency at its official central rate of 2.41 marks, a leading European economist said.
- Clear pre-election differences emerged on the thorny issue of abortion between Prime Minister John Bruton and Deputy Prime Minister Dick Spring.
- Beef baron Larry Goodman accused the Department of Agriculture of selectively leaking details of an investigation into irregularities at one of his beef plants in an attempt to damage his business.
- Tullow Oil's growing status as an international player in the oil and gas sector has set it up as a potential takeover target.
